title: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023
note: All ten supplied study-PDF pages visually reviewed. No answers are marked; audited answers are editorial inferences with cited course evidence. The crossed-out renal Q34–35 are accounted for as exclusions; the separate respiratory replacement Q34–35 are imported. Source spelling and grammar are lightly normalized, with material wording repairs documented per item. The downloadable PDF is a legible reduced-size web copy; the full-resolution original is preserved in the local archive.

questions.prompt: A decrease in oxygen pressure in the alveoli below which value (mmHg) causes hypoxia?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Unresolved: the stem conflates alveolar hypoxia, pulmonary vasoconstriction and arterial hypoxemia without naming the response or defining hypoxia. About 73 mmHg occurs in older pulmonary-vasoconstriction teaching, whereas about 60 mmHg is used for marked peripheral ventilatory sensitivity. No source answer is marked and no unique threshold can be assigned.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does NOT happen during inspiration?
options: The anterior-posterior dimension of the chest increases
The vertical dimension of the thorax increases
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The contracting diaphragm descends during inspiration, increasing vertical thoracic dimension.

questions.prompt: Where is blood flow highest in a normally oxygenated lung of a normal-weight adult man standing upright?
options: There is no gradient across the lung
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Gravity raises vascular pressure in dependent lung, so resting perfusion is highest at the base.

questions.prompt: Which product of the lung is responsible for increased bronchoconstriction and may mediate an acute asthma attack?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Histamine promotes airway smooth-muscle contraction; beta-adrenergic stimulation and VIP favor relaxation.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 4; source page 2.

questions.prompt: What is recoil pressure?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The transpulmonary pressure, Palv minus Ppl, balances elastic recoil under static conditions. Source 'plural' is normalized to pleural.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 5; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Terminal bronchioles are examples of which of the following?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Terminal bronchioles end the conducting zone and do not contain alveolar gas-exchange surfaces.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 6; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which ordering of average lung capacities at rest is true?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: For the textbook average adult values, total lung capacity exceeds vital capacity, which exceeds inspiratory capacity, which exceeds functional residual capacity.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 7; source page 3.

questions.prompt: If progressive lung disease requires increasing pressure to fill the same lung volume, how is lung compliance affected?
options: These variables do not affect lung compliance
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Compliance is the volume change divided by pressure change; requiring greater pressure for a fixed volume change means lower compliance.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 8; source page 3.

questions.prompt: If the blood supply to an alveolus is blocked, which of the following would NOT occur?
options: The ventilation-perfusion ratio would be zero
Alveolar O2 pressure (PAO2) would be greater than normal
Alveolar CO2 pressure (PACO2) would be greater than normal
The alveolar ventilation rate would be greater than normal
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Multiple options fail: if ventilation persists and perfusion is zero, V/Q tends to infinity rather than zero (A), and alveolar CO2 falls toward inspired levels rather than rising (C). Increased ventilation (D) is not guaranteed. The unmarked source cannot be assigned one answer.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 9; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which statement is FALSE about variables governing O2 diffusion across a membrane?
options: Doubling respiratory-membrane thickness halves O2 diffusion
The lower the diffusion coefficient, the higher the total diffusion
Increasing alveolar oxygen concentration increases O2 diffusion
Doubling membrane surface area doubles O2 diffusion
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: With other variables fixed, diffusion rate increases with the diffusion coefficient and area, and decreases with membrane thickness.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 10; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a form in which CO2 is transported in blood?
options: Bound to amino end groups in hemoglobin
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Carboxyhemoglobin contains carbon monoxide. CO2 forms carbamino compounds at amino groups and is also carried dissolved and as bicarbonate.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 11; source page 4.

questions.prompt: If blood contains 10 g hemoglobin per dL, what is its O2-carrying capacity in mL/dL?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Using 1.34 mL O2 per gram of hemoglobin at full saturation gives 10×1.34=13.4 mL/dL.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 12; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which gas is used to estimate lung diffusing capacity?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO binds hemoglobin rapidly, maintaining near-zero pulmonary-capillary CO pressure so alveolar CO pressure approximates the diffusion gradient.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 13; source page 4.

questions.prompt: What causes physiological shunt?
options: A decrease in ventilation-perfusion ratio (VA/Q) to zero
Admixture of pulmonary vein blood with bronchial vein blood
An increase in VA/Q ratio to 2.5 times normal
A decrease in cardiac output to half
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Both A (perfused, unventilated units) and B (bronchial venous admixture) contribute to physiological shunt. A single-best question without a narrower qualification has no unique answer.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 14; source page 4.

questions.prompt: The affinity of hemoglobin for O2 increases with which change?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Lower 2,3-DPG/BPG shifts the oxygen dissociation curve left; increased CO2, acidity and temperature shift it right.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 15; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the duration of exhalation is correct?
options: It increases with strong activation of the pneumotaxic center
It is shorter than inhalation during normal quiet respiration
It is affected by the VRG during normal respiration
It decreases when respiratory rate increases
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The intended normal-cycle comparison is D: increased breathing frequency shortens cycle time, including expiration. Quiet expiration is predominantly passive and normally lasts longer than inspiration. This is a usual breathing-pattern relation, not a universal law for deliberately altered inspiratory/expiratory ratios.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 16; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Which neurotransmitter is NOT released from glomus cells in the carotid bodies?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: VIP is the likely teaching distractor, but an absolute exclusion is not adequately established. Primary human histology found VIP immunoreactivity in glomic chief cells (PMID 1700931); primary human experiments directly demonstrate ACh and ATP release (PMID 24887113). Presence is not proof of release, but without specified species/conditions or a source key, the categorical NOT claim is held unresolved.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 17; source page 5.

questions.prompt: What change in breathing pattern follows destruction of the pneumotaxic center?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Loss of pontine inspiratory termination can prolong inspiration in the classic teaching model. The extent depends on remaining network and vagal input.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 18; source page 5.

questions.prompt: How much CO2 is expelled by the lungs each minute at rest?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The conventional resting adult example uses CO2 production/excretion of about 200 mL/min and O2 consumption of about 250 mL/min.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 19; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Why is systemic arterial PO2 (95 mmHg) lower than alveolar PO2 (104 mmHg) under normal conditions?
options: Physiological dead space at the lung apex
Venous admixture in the pulmonary circulation
V/Q less than one at the base of the lung (V/Q=0.6)
Lower compliance of systemic than pulmonary arteries
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: B is the best explanation for the textbook 104-to-95 comparison: less-oxygenated venous return mixes with pulmonary venous blood. Regional low V/Q can additionally contribute to the normal alveolar-arterial difference; it does not invalidate the broader admixture explanation.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 20; source page 5.

questions.prompt: What is the diffusion coefficient of a gas proportional to?
options: The square root of molecular weight
Solubility divided by the square root of molecular weight
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The relevant proportionality is D ∝ solubility/√molecular weight.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 21; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which respiratory variable decreases during exercise?
options: Blood flow at the top of the lungs
Blood transit time through pulmonary capillaries
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Increased cardiac output shortens pulmonary capillary transit time; recruitment and increased exchange capacity normally preserve equilibration.

questions.prompt: All of the following bones are present in the lateral wall of the nasal cavity except:
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The vomer forms part of the septum (medial wall), while the other listed bones contribute to the lateral wall.

questions.prompt: Which bone forms the medial border of the posterior opening of the nasal cavity?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The posterior border of the vomer separates the choanae medially.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 24; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which artery is found in the incisive canal?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The terminal greater palatine artery ascends through the incisive canal, where it anastomoses with the septal arterial network. This is the course emphasized in the review.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 25; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which bone participates in both the roof and medial surface of the nasal cavity?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The expected major answer is the ethmoid (cribriform roof and perpendicular septal plate), but ethmoid is absent. Small supporting crests or sphenoidal septal attachments do not resolve this badly specified single-best item. No answer is marked in the source.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 26; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which paranasal sinus opens into the superior meatus?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Posterior ethmoidal cells drain into the superior meatus; anterior ethmoid, maxillary and frontal drainage reaches the middle meatus.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 27; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the larynx is correct?
options: The lower chamber of the laryngeal cavity is called the vestibule
The vocal ligament is on the upper free side of the quadrangular membrane
The vocal fold lies at the top of the arytenoid cartilage
True vocal folds form the lower boundary of the middle chamber of the laryngeal cavity
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The middle chamber is between the vestibular and true vocal folds; the vocal folds form its lower limit. The source's 'quadrat membrane' is normalized to quadrangular membrane.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 28; source page 7.

questions.prompt: All of the following statements are correct except:
options: Vocal cartilages are near the midline during swallowing
Arytenoid cartilages adduct during deep breathing
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Deep inspiration requires widening of the rima glottidis through abduction, not adduction. Source option C says 'vocal cartilages'; its intended airway-closure idea is retained without inventing another option.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 29; source page 7.

questions.prompt: All of the following statements are correct except:
options: The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve supplies the upper part of the laryngeal cavity
The transverse arytenoid is the only unpaired intrinsic laryngeal muscle
Recurrent laryngeal nerves innervate the transverse arytenoid muscle
The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve passes through the thyrohyoid membrane
sourceOptions: The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve is responsible for the upper part of the laryngeal cavity.
The transverse arytenoid muscle is the only unpaired intrinsic muscle of the larynx
Laryngeal recurrent nerves innervate the transvers pyramidal muscles in the larynx
The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve passes through the hole of the thyrohyoid membrane
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The internal, not external, superior laryngeal branch pierces the thyrohyoid membrane. Practice options contain an explicit editorial correction: source option C's phrase 'transvers pyramidal muscles' is interpreted as transverse arytenoid from the adjacent laryngeal context. All four original printed choices are preserved in sourceOptions; the corrected practice wording is not a literal source transcription.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 30; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is part of the thyroarytenoid muscle?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Vocalis is the medial portion of thyroarytenoid. The source additionally prints 'Vecalis muscle' in the stem; this apparent answer leakage is omitted from the cleaned question and recorded here.

questions.prompt: The uncinate process is present in which bone?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The uncinate process projects from the ethmoidal labyrinth and helps define drainage pathways of the middle meatus.

questions.prompt: The nasopalatine nerve is a branch of which nerve?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Nasopalatine sensory fibers arise from V2 through the pterygopalatine ganglion pathway.

questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: During the canalicular period, terminal bronchioles subdivide into respiratory bronchioles and alveolar ducts. This replacement respiratory Q34 supersedes the visibly crossed-out renal Q34 on page 8.

questions.subject: embryology

questions.prompt: In which of the following is the histological structure of the vocal cord observed?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The stem asks for vocal-cord location but offers nasal zones and the pharynx. If it intended an epithelial resemblance, that qualification and the type of vocal fold are missing. No unique answer is supportable from the printed item.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 36; source page 10.

questions.prompt: Which part of lung tissue has simple squamous cells?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The alveolar gas-exchange surface is largely covered by attenuated simple squamous type I pneumocytes.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 37; source page 10.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the alveolar macrophage of the lung?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The accepted term is alveolar macrophage/dust cell, which is absent. Types I and II are epithelial pneumocytes; nonstandard type III/IV labels are not substituted for macrophages without an explicit course definition.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 38; source page 10.

questions.prompt: Where are the mucous and serous glands located in the tracheal wall?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Tracheal seromucous glands chiefly occupy the submucosa. The source's 'Mucosa & Serosa Gland' wording is normalized to mucous and serous glands.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 2, 2023; printed question 39; source page 10.

questions.prompt: In which region are unicellular glands (goblet cells) observed?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Here 'respiratory zone' denotes nasal respiratory mucosa, as contrasted with the vestibule. It must not be confused with the distal pulmonary gas-exchange zone, which normally lacks goblet cells.
